name: Bai
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into 2-inch chunks (or substitute with smoked pork for deeper flavor)
1 cup fermented bamboo shoots (tuai), rinsed and drained
2 cups mixed local greens (such as mustard leaves, spinach, or chard), roughly chopped
4-5 fresh turmeric leaves (or 1 tsp turmeric powder if unavailable)
1 tsp fermented fish (ngari) or 2 tbsp fish sauce (optional, for umami)
instructions: 1. In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat mustard oil over medium-high heat. Add sliced onions and sauté until golden brown, about 5 minutes.
2. Add minced garlic and julienned ginger; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add pork chunks and sear on all sides until lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.

4. Pour in water or stock, add fermented bamboo shoots, turmeric leaves, green chillies, and fermented fish (if using). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes or until pork is tender.
5. Add the mixed greens and stir gently. Continue to simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes until greens are wilted and flavors meld.
6. Season with salt to taste. Remove turmeric leaves before serving (or leave as garnish). Serve hot with steamed rice.
description: A smoky, heart-warming embrace of fermented bamboo and mountain herbs, simmered in the misty hills of Mizoram.
